EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
American Honda Pledges $3 Billion in Investments in the US Focused on Hybrids via Multiple Facilitie
6 photos
Photo: Honda
Honda recently said that it wants to "meet growing customer demand for hybrid vehicles in North America," so it's now building a brand-new auto plant in Central Ohio, among other things.
The Japanese automaker’s local subsidiary, American Honda , recently achieved its best October sales month in six years following a delivery jump of eight percent and stands at a five-percent growth rate after ten months and 1,269,213 total deliveries. The namesake Honda brand took the lion’s share, of course, rising more than nine percent in October and over five percent during the ten months to almost 1.155 million units.
Honda not long ago abandoned plans that almost came to fruition to bring new EV models built in-house to America, plus a collaboration with Sony for the Afeela brand, and took a massive hit across the ledgers. But they’re striving to get past that moment to refocus their business plans on hybrids, which are now seen as a better fit for North America.
The new plans will include the upcoming auto plant in Central Ohio, creating more than 2,000 new American jobs and increasing local production capacity to around 1.3 million vehicles annually. The new facility will be built alongside the existing Ohio manufacturing operations and is expected to start operations in 2029 (pending final government approvals). But the new factory isn’t coming alone.
It’s actually part of a broader set of investments that will positively impact the Honda operations in Ohio, Alabama, and Georgia, expanding and strengthening the integrated US production network to boost production and productivity of both HEVs and the engines and hybrid systems that power them.
"As Honda approaches 50 years of building products close to our customers in America, we are making one of the most significant commitments in our history to position Honda for the next 50 years,” said Bob Nelson, executive vice president of American Honda Motor Co., Inc. “These investments strengthen America’s role as a cornerstone of Honda’s global future and reflect our confidence in our more than 30,000 Honda associates and the strength of American manufacturing.”
Both Honda and Acura products will be covered by the new facilities, “including hybrid-electric vehicles and multiple new models currently under development by Honda R&D operations in the US.”
Back in May 2026, Honda revealed it will seek to introduce 15 new Honda and Acura hybrid models globally by 2030, with North America being the primary market for many of them. At the end of the investment road, Honda will have an integrated production capacity of around 1.3 million vehicles in the US and no less than 1.9 million in total across North America.
The investment numbers include the $3 billion for the new Ohio auto plant, 240k units in annual capacity for the new facility, a 250-percent increase in hybrid powertrain system capacity in Ohio, and 99% localized North American production for all Honda and Acura models purchased in the US back in 2025.
